name: AI in Medical, Legal and Regulatory Review
title: AI in Medical, Legal and Regulatory Review
answer: Promotional materials must pass medical, legal and regulatory review before use, and AI now pre-checks them, flagging spelling errors, prohibited phrases, missing safety warnings and other guideline breaches so reviewers start from a cleaner draft. Veeva has built such checks into its PromoMats content system.

reading.body:
AI pre-checks promotional materials for spelling errors, prohibited phrases and missing safety warnings, so medical, legal and regulatory reviewers start from a cleaner draft.

The pattern is triage. The mechanical defects in a promotional document are finite and enumerable: a misspelling, a phrase the guidelines forbid, a safety warning that should be present and is not. Software can find those against a rule set. What it cannot settle is whether a claim is adequately supported or whether the fair balance between benefit and risk is right, and those are the questions that consume reviewer time. Veeva has built these checks into its PromoMats content system, which places the review inside the same system that holds the content rather than beside it.

For AI specifically, this is a narrow and honest use of the technology. It is not generating the promotional material and not approving it. It is a filter positioned before human sign-off, which means its failure mode is a missed flag rather than a wrong claim reaching the market. The value is throughput: fewer review cycles spent on typos and boilerplate warnings, more spent on judgement.

The data covers one vendor and one class of checks. It does not say how accurate the flagging is, how many review cycles it removes, or whether regulators accept it as anything more than an internal aid. It also does not describe the compute behind it, and nothing here suggests these checks are constrained by compute, buildings or power. This is a software feature, not a grid story.

sections.body: Let AI catch the mechanical issues and keep reviewers on claims and fair balance, where judgement matters.
